_comment: Field battles: an army holding a hex fights any horde whose route crosses it. Ambush: on `ambush.terrain`, with the army in place `ambush.prepMinutes` game minutes before the horde arrives, the defenders' first round hits `ambush.bonus` harder and the horde fights it without its stance. Choke point: a passable hex with at least `choke.minBlockedNeighbors` impassable neighbours; attackers hit `choke.attackerFactor` as hard there, and Hold the Line gains `choke.holdTheLineDefense` defense. River: a horde that crossed a river into the hex it fights in (over a bridge; nothing crosses elsewhere) hits `river.attackerFactor` as hard, at walls or in the field. Forts are built within `fort.range` hexes of a village and give armies holding them `fort.defenseBonus` defense; each keeps up to `fort.grainCapacity` grain. Supply points are built like forts (within `supplyPoint.range` hexes, paid from the village, standing after `supplyPoint.buildSeconds`) and keep up to `supplyPoint.grainCapacity` grain, but give no defense. An army that arrives at or stands on a fort or supply point fills up from its grain as it would in a village, and a standing army can leave grain there from its own supply. A horde that passes within its raid reach of a supply point (built or being built) burns it, grain and all, unless an army stands on it; forts keep their grain behind their walls. Bridges are built over a river edge within `bridge.range` hexes of a village (game seconds, divided by world speed); until one stands nothing crosses there, hordes included. Roads are built between two neighbouring hexes within `road.range` of a village, (a road into impassable land with a `roadMoveCost`, a mountain pass, costs `mountainFactor` times as much and takes `mountainFactor` times as long, every level), and improved twice more: each of `road.levels` is paid from the village and done after its `buildSeconds`, and moving along a road costs its level's `factor` of the terrain (a road being improved keeps its level until the work is done), for players and the human hordes alike, but the Monsters of the North keep off them. An outpost joined to its village by roads gathers more: over the fewest road steps between them (of those, the best built), the average of each step's level `outpostBonus` is added to its yield. Terraforming (`terraform`): a village reshapes the land within `range` hexes of it, on a hex with no village, outpost, fort, camp or site and no other work under way there: each of `actions` turns the terrain named in `from` into the one it maps to, is paid at once (`cost`, mostly grain to feed the workers) and done after `hours` game hours (divided by world speed); clearing a forest also brings its timber, levelling hills their stone (`gain`), to the village. A work with `fire` sets the forest alight: while it burns (its `hours`) nothing can enter the hex, armies, caravans, scouts and hordes alike (a horde already on its way keeps its route); with `spreadChance` the fire spreads to each neighbouring hex it could burn (the land in `from`, but never a settlement, which stops it) `spreadHours` later, at most `generations` hexes from where it was set, burning any outpost (to ruins), fort, supply point or camp there; a burnt hex becomes what `from` names, and its timber is lost. Wagon fort: an army holding open ground (no fort, supply point or village) with wagons (units.json `wagon`) can draw them into a ring, ready after `wagonFort.setupMinutes` game minutes; it gives `wagonFort.bonusPerWagon` defense for each wagon per `wagonFort.menPerWagon` soldiers (wagons x bonusPerWagon / ceil(soldiers / menPerWagon)), at most `wagonFort.maxBonus`, and breaks up when the army moves.

clear.name: Clear the forest
clear.description: Fell the trees for the land beneath: forest becomes plains, wooded hills bare hills, and the timber comes home.

plant.name: Plant trees
plant.description: Sow a wood: plains become forest, hills wooded hills, for woodcutters and outposts to come. Nothing comes home.

drain.name: Drain the swamp
drain.description: Dig ditches until the swamp is dry plains. Nothing comes home.

level.name: Level the hills
level.description: Cut the hills down to plains; the stone comes home.

burn.name: Burn the forest
burn.description: Set the forest alight: nothing gets through while it burns, and the fire may spread to the trees around it, burning what stands there. Forest becomes plains, wooded hills bare hills; the timber is lost.
